title: The Engineer's Degree and the Federation: Santiago, the Sierra Cristal, and Forty-Seven Years in One Office
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: born in the lawyer's house
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both English Wikipedia and EcuRed, which agree on the date, the city and the parents. They do not agree on the children: English Wikipedia lists four siblings, Nilsa, Iván, Sonia and José; EcuRed lists five, adding Liliana. No civil register was reached and the count is left open. The coordinate is the corpus's Santiago pin, not a street address, which no source reached supplies
stops.campa: The house belongs to José Espín, a lawyer with money and standing in Oriente, and to Margarita Guillois. Their daughter is born on the seventh of April into a household that keeps ballet lessons, French, and the habits of the Santiago professional class. Outside it the city is a port of sugar and nickel and men who work four months of the year, and the two facts sit a few streets apart without touching. She will spend twenty-two years on the inside of that arrangement. The house itself will end up sheltering men with guns.
suggested_refs: Civil registration records for Santiago de Cuba, April 1930, which would settle the four-versus-five sibling question

stops.name: Academia Pérez-Peña, Santiago de Cuba: the first school
stops.date_confidence: the school is attested by English Wikipedia and EcuRed; no enrolment year is given anywhere reached, and 1936 is an inference from her age with January as the house default. The coordinate is approximate to the school's quarter of the city
stops.campa: She is sent to the Academia Pérez-Peña for her letters, a private school for the daughters of families who can pay. She learns to read in a province where a large share of her contemporaries never will. The school's own enrolment records were not reachable, so the year on this stop is inferred from her age. About the household itself the fullest account is a Cuban state encyclopedia's, written half a century later, describing a childhood home built on ethics, austerity and culture.
suggested_refs: Enrolment and class records of the Academia Pérez-Peña, Santiago de Cuba, 1930s

stops.name: Colegio Sagrado Corazón, Santiago de Cuba: the bachillerato
stops.date_confidence: the bachillerato en ciencias of 1948 is attested by EcuRed; the month is not given and January is the house default. The ballet and singing at the Asociación Pro-Arte Cubano are attested by both encyclopedias, but no address or coordinate for the Pro-Arte building in Santiago was reached, so this stop stands on the school
stops.campa: The Sagrado Corazón carries her to the bachillerato in sciences, taken in 1948. Alongside the school she studies ballet and singing at the Asociación Pro-Arte Cubano, whose Santiago halls in these years bring dancers and singers through for an audience of a few hundred families. No address for the Pro-Arte building was reached, so this stop stands on the school instead. She is eighteen, trained in the five positions and in chemistry. It is the chemistry she chooses.
suggested_refs: The Asociación Pro-Arte Cubano's Santiago de Cuba programmes of the 1940s

stops.name: Universidad de Oriente, Santiago de Cuba: chemical engineering
stops.date_confidence: the 1950 enrolment is attested by English Wikipedia and EcuRed; the month is not given and January is the house default. The coordinate is corrected: the dossier behind this file gave 20.0092 / -75.8285, and Spanish Wikipedia's article on the university gives 20 degrees 02 minutes 36 seconds north, 75 degrees 49 minutes 02 seconds west, about four kilometres away
stops.campa: The university is four years old when she enrolls, the first in the eastern provinces, founded so that Oriente need not send its children to Havana. She takes chemical engineering, a faculty with almost no women in it anywhere on the island. The classrooms hold daughters of the Santiago professional families beside scholarship boys up from the sugar districts, and the politics comes in through the door with the second group. She sings in the university choir. She captains the volleyball team.
suggested_refs: Faculty of Chemical Engineering records, Universidad de Oriente, 1950-1954

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the tenth of March
stops.date_confidence: the coup is attested to the day. Her participation in the university demonstrations that followed is attested by Spanish Wikipedia and EcuRed, neither of which names a specific date, march, or arrest, so the coup date stands for the whole episode
stops.campa: Fulgencio Batista takes the government before dawn on the tenth of March, cancelling an election he was going to lose. In Santiago the university students go into the street, and Espín is among them: twenty-one, an engineering student, with no party and no organisation behind her. Which march, which day, whether she was ever picked up: none of the sources reached will say, and they record only that she took part. The demonstrations are broken up. The coup holds. The university keeps meeting.
suggested_refs: Student movement records at the Universidad de Oriente following the coup of 10 March 1952

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the house takes in the men from Moncada
stops.date_confidence: the assault is attested to the day. That the Espín family residence sheltered attackers in flight is Spanish Wikipedia's detail, carried without a document or an attacker's own testimony behind it and treated as reconstruction. The pin is the family house at the corpus's Santiago coordinate, not the barracks, which she did not go near; the barracks stand at 20.0264 / -75.8192
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of July a little over a hundred fighters attack the Moncada barracks across the city and lose. Those who get out run through Santiago looking for doors that will open, and the Espín house, a lawyer's house, respectable, above suspicion, is one of the doors that opens. The daughter of the house is twenty-three years old and has joined nothing. Her connection to the assault, on this day, is that she lives at an address the survivors of it can reach on foot.
suggested_refs: fidel_castro.journey.json, stop 'Moncada Barracks, Santiago de Cuba: the assault', for the attack itself

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: Acción Revolucionaria Oriental
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Spanish Wikipedia places the meeting with Frank País in Santiago shortly after the Moncada attack of 26 July 1953; no day is given and August is a default inside that window. The chronology behind this file added a garbled Acción Nacional Revolucionaria as a predecessor organisation and put Havana in the place field; neither has a source and neither is used
stops.campa: Through the university group Acción Revolucionaria Oriental she meets Frank País García, a teacher's son from this city, twenty years old, already the best organiser in the province. He will fold the group into the Movement that names itself after the Moncada date. She becomes his collaborator and stays it for four years, which is the rest of his life. The coordinate here is the university quarter where the group met; no meeting house is named in anything reached.
suggested_refs: Acción Revolucionaria Oriental and its absorption into the Movimiento 26 de Julio

stops.name: Universidad de Oriente, Santiago de Cuba: the last examination
stops.date_confidence: EcuRed is explicit: el 14 de julio realiza el último examen, and dates the qualification to 1954. The dossier behind this file contradicts itself here, its chronology giving 14 July 1955 and its geography giving 14 July 1954, the same day and month a year apart. EcuRed settles it at 1954, and the American year moves back accordingly
stops.campa: On the fourteenth of July she sits the last examination and takes the degree in industrial chemical engineering, one of the first two women in Cuba to hold it. She is twenty-four. Her father has paid for an education meant to end in a laboratory or a refinery office. EcuRed dates the examination to the day and the qualification to 1954, against a 1955 that appears in the working material behind this file and is not carried here. What the degree also buys is a passport, a professional reason to travel abroad, and fluent technical English.
suggested_refs: Degree records of the Universidad de Oriente, July 1954, naming the first two Cuban women qualified in industrial chemical engineering

stops.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge: one semester
stops.date_confidence: single-source on the institution. English Wikipedia names MIT and one semester completed; EcuRed says only a postgraduate course in the United States and names no school, so the MIT identification is reconstruction rather than attestation. The year follows from the corrected July 1954 degree date; September is a default for the start of an academic year. The coordinate is the corpus's existing Cambridge pin
stops.campa: Her father sends her north for postgraduate work in chemical engineering, distance being the standard family remedy for a daughter who has started going to demonstrations. She spends a Massachusetts winter among students for whom politics is an argument rather than a police matter. English Wikipedia names the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and one semester finished; EcuRed says only that she went to the United States for a postgraduate course, and names nothing. She does not stay for the second term.
suggested_refs: MIT registrar records for the academic year 1954-1955, which would confirm or remove the single-source identification
sources: adi_shamir.journey.json, stop 'Cambridge, the couch and the mathematics textbook', for the canonical coordinate

stops.name: Mexico City: the instructions
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested by both English and Spanish Wikipedia; no month is given and January is the house default. The date sits loosely inside the Mexican exile period, which ran from mid-1955 to the Granma sailing of 25 November 1956
stops.campa: Coming home from the United States she goes by way of Mexico, where the men who survived Moncada are training in rented houses under the eye of the Mexican police. She meets Fidel Castro there, and Raúl Castro, and formally joins the Twenty-sixth of July Movement. An engineer with an American visa, a professional reason to travel and unaccented English is the courier an exile command needs. The year is attested and the month is not, and what was agreed in the room is recorded nowhere reached. She leaves the city with instructions for Frank País.
suggested_refs: The Movimiento 26 de Julio exile organisation in Mexico City, 1955-1956

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the courier
stops.date_confidence: the courier and liaison role is attested by English Wikipedia for 1956, without dates for individual journeys; June is a default inside the year. The stop is pinned at the Santiago end of a route whose other end is Mexico City
stops.campa: She carries messages between the exile command in Mexico and the underground Frank País runs in Santiago, and she handles the Movement's contacts in English. The traffic runs in both directions for most of a year. What was in the messages is not preserved in anything reached; only the fact of the route, and who was standing at each end of it. Her cover is her own biography: a chemical engineer from a good family, twenty-six years old, travelling on business that a customs officer has no reason to question.
suggested_refs: Correspondence between the Mexican exile leadership and the Oriente underground, 1956

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the thirtieth of November
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Spanish Wikipedia and EcuRed. The use of the family residence as a Movement operational address is English Wikipedia's claim, carried as reconstruction with no document behind it
stops.campa: On the thirtieth of November the Movement rises inside Santiago in red and black armbands, attacking the police headquarters and the maritime police, to pull Batista's forces off the coast while the Granma comes in. By now her house is an operational address of the underground, used for meetings, for relaying messages and for shelter, on the reasoning that a chemical engineer's family home is the last place the police will look. That last claim rests on one encyclopedia and no document. The rising is put down within the day. The landing goes badly anyway.
suggested_refs: fidel_castro.journey.json, stop 'Playa Las Coloradas: not a landing but a shipwreck', for the landing the rising was timed to cover

stops.name: Sierra Maestra: the correspondent from New York
stops.date_confidence: the Matthews interview is attested to 17 February 1957; her role in it is not settled. EcuRed places her among those who guided him to Castro; English Wikipedia has her interpreting at a press interview and arranging an intelligence contact around this period. The two accounts are not reconciled here. The location is reconstruction: the dossier pinned the Comandancia de La Plata, which was not established until 1958, so the corpus's regional Sierra Maestra coordinate is used and the exact site is recorded as undetermined
stops.campa: Herbert Matthews of the New York Times is brought up into the mountains in February and comes down with the dispatch that tells the world Fidel Castro is alive, which Batista's government has spent two months denying. EcuRed puts Espín among the people who got him there. English Wikipedia has her instead interpreting at a Castro press interview and arranging an intelligence contact in roughly this period. The accounts do not agree on the episode or on her part in it, and they are left disagreeing.
suggested_refs: Herbert Matthews, 'Cuban Rebel Is Visited in Hideout', The New York Times, 24 February 1957
che_guevara.journey.json, segment 'Granma and the Sierra Maestra'

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: coordinator of the province
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed: el 20 de julio de 1957, Vilma Espín asciende a la dirección de la lucha como coordinadora provincial del MR-26-7. This corrects both lenses of the dossier behind this file, which dated the appointment to 31 July or to August 1957 and made it a consequence of Frank País's death. País was alive on 20 July and was killed on 30 July
stops.campa: On the twentieth of July she is made provincial coordinator of the Twenty-sixth of July Movement for Oriente: the ranking clandestine officer in the province, responsible for arms, safe houses, message routes, money, and the people who carry all four. She is twenty-seven. The usual telling has her rise to the post when Frank País was killed, which reverses the order. País is alive and running the underground alongside her on the day she takes it. He has ten days left.
suggested_refs: Movimiento 26 de Julio provincial command records for Oriente, July 1957

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the day they kill Frank País
stops.date_confidence: the killing is attested to 30 July 1957, not 31 July as the chronology behind this file had it. Spanish Wikipedia's article on País places it in the Callejón del Muro, after a beating on calle San Germán, with Raúl Pujol killed alongside him. The dossier's San Agustín neighborhood has no source and is dropped; no verified coordinate for the Callejón del Muro was obtained, so the city pin is used
stops.campa: On the thirtieth of July the police take Frank País and Raúl Pujol off the street, beat them on calle San Germán, and shoot them in an alley called the Callejón del Muro, for which no verified coordinate was obtained. Espín has been provincial coordinator for ten days and now holds the network alone. She is twenty-seven. Santiago answers with a strike, and the city walks behind the coffins; the footage of that funeral does the Movement more good in Oriente than any operation of the year.
suggested_refs: The Callejón del Muro, Santiago de Cuba, and the funeral of Frank País, 31 July 1957

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the man from the Central Intelligence Agency
stops.date_confidence: the meeting is dated only to 1957 or 1958 by the source, and January 1958 is a placeholder inside that window. The quotation is one remove from its primary text: Tom Gjelten's book could not be opened in this session, and the wording was confirmed only through the English Wikipedia citation of it
stops.campa: Pepín Bosch, an executive of the Bacardi company, arranges a meeting between the Movement and Lyman Kirkpatrick, inspector general of the Central Intelligence Agency, and Espín speaks for the underground. It is one of the few occasions in these years when what she said in a room survives in any form. Gjelten's book could not be opened here, and the wording reaches this file at one remove from its source. She is asked what the rebels want, and answers: what you Americans have, clean politics and a clean police system.
stops.quote: what you Americans have: clean politics and a clean police system.
stops.quote_source: Vilma Espín to CIA Inspector General Lyman Kirkpatrick, 1957 or 1958, quoted in Tom Gjelten, Bacardi and the Long Fight for Cuba (Penguin, 2008)
suggested_refs: Tom Gjelten, Bacardi and the Long Fight for Cuba: The Biography of a Cause (Penguin, 2008)

stops.name: Mayarí Arriba, Sierra Cristal: into the Second Front
stops.date_confidence: the June 1958 entry and the six months of service under Raúl Castro are attested by Spanish Wikipedia, EcuRed and English Wikipedia; the day is not given and the first is the house default. The coordinate is corrected to the Segundo Frente municipal seat at Mayarí Arriba as given by English Wikipedia; the dossier's 20.4667 / -75.6333 lies about eleven kilometres northwest. The front operated in the Sierra Cristal, not the Sierra Maestra, which the dossier conflates in two places
stops.campa: In June she leaves the city and goes up into the Sierra Cristal, to the Second Eastern Front, founded in March at Piloto del Medio and commanded by Raúl Castro. The front is a government as much as a column: schools, a hospital, courts, a peasant congress, an airstrip. She serves six months in it. Asked long afterwards to compare the mountain with hiding from the police in Santiago, she prefers the mountain; her words reach the record only in paraphrase, and are not quoted here as hers.
suggested_refs: The Segundo Frente Oriental Frank País, founded 11 March 1958 at Piloto del Medio

stops.name: Segundo Frente Oriental: the North Americans at Moa and Nicaro
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed, which names her interpreting role and the operation. The outcome of the affair is not carried in any source reached for this file. The coordinate is the front's command seat at Mayarí Arriba, not the nickel installations at Moa and Nicaro, for which no verified coordinate was obtained
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of June the front takes American servicemen and technicians off the nickel installations at Moa and Nicaro and holds them in the mountains. Espín interprets for the Second Front command. The technical English her father paid for, meant for a refinery office, is spent instead on negotiations over prisoners in a guerrilla camp. EcuRed gives her role and the date and stops there. Whether the men walked out, were traded, or were handed to an intermediary, no source reached says.
suggested_refs: The Moa and Nicaro nickel installations and the Rebel Army hostage operation of June 1958

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the first of January
stops.date_confidence: the balcony speech is attested by Spanish Wikipedia, which notes it was delivered late on the night of 1-2 January. Her personal presence in the square is not attested in anything reached and is reconstruction; only her presence in the city is secure. The coordinate is the corpus's Santiago pin. Parque Céspedes itself lies about 850 metres west, at 20.0215 / -75.8295
stops.campa: Batista's plane leaves Havana in the dark, and by night Fidel Castro is on the balcony of the city hall on Parque Céspedes telling Santiago that the revolution has begun. Espín is twenty-eight. She has spent six of the last eight years in this city working against the government that fell this morning, first as a courier, then as the officer who ran the province. Whether she stood in the square that night is not written down anywhere reached. A crowd is not a document.
suggested_refs: fidel_castro.journey.json, stop 'Santiago de Cuba: the revolution begins now'
sources: General accounts of 1 January 1959 in Santiago de Cuba

stops.name: Havana: the move to the capital
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. English Wikipedia records the relocation to Havana in early January 1959 without a date; the tenth is a placeholder set just after the caravan's arrival at Camp Columbia on the eighth. The coordinate is the corpus's Havana pin for the seat of government
stops.campa: The rebel columns go west along the length of the island and the government reassembles itself in Havana, in requisitioned hotels and army camps. Espín moves with it. Everything she has done up to this month, the schools, the degree, the underground, the mountain, has happened inside a hundred and fifty kilometres of the house she was born in. The date here is a placeholder set just after the caravan reached Camp Columbia; the sources give only early January. She has never lived in the capital.
suggested_refs: fidel_castro.journey.json, stop 'Havana: Camp Columbia and the doves', for the caravan's arrival

stops.name: Havana: the marriage to Raúl Castro
stops.date_confidence: the date of 26 January 1959 is attested by English Wikipedia's article on Raúl Castro. The venue is not given in any source reached, and the city is contested: the geography of this dossier pins Havana while stating the venue unknown, and its interlock lens places the wedding in Santiago de Cuba. Neither is documented and the disagreement is left standing
stops.campa: On the twenty-sixth of January, three and a half weeks after the government falls, she marries Raúl Castro Ruz, who commanded the front she fought in. No source reached names the church, the house, or the officiant, and one reading of the record puts the ceremony in Santiago rather than Havana. Mariela, the younger daughter, will spend her own career arguing for sexual rights inside the institutions her mother is about to build. The four children are Deborah, Mariela, Nilsa and Alejandro.
suggested_refs: A marriage register for January 1959 that would settle the venue and the city

stops.name: Havana: first lady of a country with no such office
stops.date_confidence: English Wikipedia dates her informal standing as de facto First Lady from 16 February 1959, the day Fidel Castro was sworn in as prime minister. The role is a reference-work convention rather than a Cuban office, and no Cuban source reached uses the term
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of February Fidel Castro is sworn in as prime minister, and from that date the English-language reference works begin counting Espín as Cuba's de facto first lady, a position the republic does not have and the revolution does not recognise. She is the wife of the head of the armed forces and the sister-in-law of the head of government. What she does with the standing is not receive guests: within eighteen months she has an organisation of her own. No Cuban source reached uses the phrase first lady about her at all.
suggested_refs: fidel_castro.journey.json, stop 'Havana: sworn in as prime minister'

stops.name: Havana: the agrarian reform draft and the columnist
stops.date_confidence: the clipping is undated. The 1999 date visible in the archive.org metadata is the release date of the file, not the column's, and the placement in May 1959 is inferred from the agrarian reform content, matching the corpus's date for the First Agrarian Reform Law. The document is not a CIA assessment: it is a clipping of Drew Pearson's syndicated column filed in the agency's press series, so Pearson is reporting what a CIA report allegedly said
stops.campa: A clipping in the agency's press files, Drew Pearson's Washington Merry-Go-Round under the headline CIA Data Cited Against Castro, lists Espín among five drafters of the agrarian reform bill alongside Ernesto Che Guevara, Raúl Castro, Antonio Núñez Jiménez and Pinos Santos. The same column calls her the sister of a noted French Communist and apparently a Communist herself. That is a period allegation of doubtful accuracy, set down here as what was being said about her in Washington and not as a fact about her family.
stops.quote: the sister of a noted French Communist and apparently a Communist herself
stops.quote_source: Drew Pearson, 'Washington Merry-Go-Round: CIA Data Cited Against Castro', syndicated column, clipped in CIA Reading Room record CIA-RDP75-00149R000200580013-6

stops.name: Santiago, Chile: the first congress
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Spanish Wikipedia records that she led the Cuban delegation to the First Latin American Congress on Women and Children in 1959; no month, no dates, no delegation list. November is a default placed late in the year, and the stop's real position inside 1959 is unknown. The congress's own proceedings were not located
stops.campa: She leads the Cuban delegation to the First Latin American Congress on Women and Children, the first time she stands in a foreign hall as the representative of a government rather than as a courier for a movement. Spanish Wikipedia carries the trip in a single clause and gives no month, which is why the date here sits late in the year for want of anywhere better to put it. The size of the delegation, its resolutions, what Cuba proposed and whether the hall adopted any of it: gaps, all four.
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the First Latin American Congress on Women and Children, Santiago de Chile, 1959

stops.name: Habana Libre, Havana: the Federation
stops.date_confidence: the founding date of 23 August 1960 and her presidency until her death are attested by English Wikipedia, Spanish Wikipedia and EcuRed together. The venue is reconstruction: the hotel is the dossier's suggestion and no source reached names the hall. The coordinate is the corpus's existing Habana Libre pin
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of August the island's existing women's organisations are merged into one, the Federación de Mujeres Cubanas, and Espín is its president. She will hold the post for forty-six years and ten months and die in it. The Federation is not a lobby and does not petition the state; it is an arm of the state, chartered to move women into wage work, literacy campaigns, militias, and the emergency medical brigades it raises within months of its founding. Which hall the founding congress met in, no source reached says.
suggested_refs: Founding congress records of the Federación de Mujeres Cubanas, August 1960
celia_sanchez.journey.json, stop 'Habana Libre: the twenty-third floor', for the canonical coordinate

stops.name: Havana: the children's circles
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Spanish Wikipedia summarises the círculos infantiles and the retraining programmes over a 1961-1965 span with no founding date; January 1961 is the house default at the start of that range. No enrolment figure, budget or programme record was reached, and the coordinate is approximate to the ministries quarter of Havana
stops.campa: The Federation opens the círculos infantiles, state day nurseries, on the plain reasoning that a woman cannot take a factory shift while holding a child. Both this and what follows reach the file as a Spanish Wikipedia summary and nothing more: no enrolment numbers, no budgets, no programme records, no founding date inside the 1961 to 1965 span. It also runs literacy and retraining courses for former prostitutes, whom the revolutionary government treats as a category to be abolished rather than a population to be policed.
suggested_refs: FMC records of the círculos infantiles programme, 1961-1965

stops.name: Havana: the Central Committee
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested by English Wikipedia, Spanish Wikipedia and EcuRed; the party was constituted in October 1965 but no source reached gives her a date within the year, so January is the house default
stops.campa: The Communist Party of Cuba is constituted and she is named to its Central Committee at the founding, one of very few women in the body. The party absorbs the Movement she joined in a Mexico City safe house nine years earlier, and the Federation she runs becomes one of the mass organisations attached to it. She reached the seat through a provincial coordinator's post held in a city where being found out meant being shot in an alley. Her seat is not her husband's. No source reached gives a date within the year.
suggested_refs: Founding Central Committee membership lists of the Partido Comunista de Cuba, October 1965

stops.name: Havana: the Ministry of Food Industry
stops.date_confidence: the year and the post are attested by English Wikipedia, which says nothing about what she did in it; the month is not given and January is the house default. Ministry records for the period were not located. The coordinate is approximate to the ministries quarter of Havana
stops.campa: She is made director of industrial development at the Ministry of Food Industry, a technical post: process, plant, output, the yield of a line. The chemical engineering her father bought in order to keep her out of politics is at last used for the thing it was trained for, inside the government that the politics produced. English Wikipedia gives the year and the title. It gives nothing else, and the ministry's own records were not reachable, so what she actually did there is unknown.
suggested_refs: Ministerio de la Industria Alimenticia records, 1969-1971

stops.name: Havana: the Institute of Childcare
stops.date_confidence: the year of the childcare institute presidency and the 1967-1971 span of the Commission for Social Prevention are both attested by English Wikipedia; neither carries a month, and January is the house default. The coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: She takes the presidency of the national childcare institute and extends the nursery network across the provinces. For the four years before it she chaired the Commission for Social Prevention, the body handling delinquency, abandonment and the domestic wreckage that the sources describe only in the abstract. Between the Federation, the commission and the institute she now holds most of the levers the Cuban state possesses for reaching inside a household and rearranging what is in it.
suggested_refs: Instituto de la Infancia records, 1971 onward

stops.name: Havana: the Family Code
stops.date_confidence: the year and her role as principal architect and public champion are attested by English and Spanish Wikipedia; no promulgation date was carried in the material behind this file, so month and day are house defaults
stops.campa: The Código de Familia is written into law with Espín as its principal public advocate. Article by article it obliges a husband whose wife works outside the home to take half the housework and half the care of the children, and makes the obligation something a divorce court can weigh. Nothing like it exists elsewhere in Latin America. Cuban households do not rearrange themselves on the morning of promulgation, and the Federation spends the next thirty years saying so in public.
suggested_refs: The Cuban Código de Familia of 1975, articles on shared domestic responsibility

stops.name: Mexico City: the First World Conference on Women
stops.date_confidence: Spanish Wikipedia's summary of her international representation names the conference and the year and nothing else. June is a default inside the year. No text of any Cuban intervention at the conference was located
stops.campa: The United Nations holds its first world conference on women in Mexico City and she leads the Cuban delegation. Nineteen years earlier she came through this city as a courier collecting instructions from men living under false names in rented houses. She returns to it at the head of a delegation, carrying a family code adopted the same year, and the code is what she has to exhibit. What she said from the floor is not in anything reached for this file.
suggested_refs: Report of the World Conference of the International Women's Year, Mexico City, 1975

stops.name: Havana: the Order Ana Betancourt
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed, which gives it as the Orden Ana Betancourt. The chronology behind this file called it a medal; EcuRed calls it an order, and the order is used. The date is the Federation's fifteenth anniversary
stops.campa: On the Federation's fifteenth anniversary, to the day, the state gives her the Orden Ana Betancourt. EcuRed records it as an order rather than a medal, and gives the date and nothing else about the occasion. Espín is forty-five and has run the organisation being celebrated since the day it was founded. The name on the order is that of the nineteenth-century Cuban woman who asked the men writing the republic's first constitution to free women as well as slaves.
suggested_refs: The Orden Ana Betancourt and its statute

stops.name: Palacio de la Revolución, Havana: the constitution of 1976
stops.date_confidence: the deputyship in the first legislature of the National Assembly is attested by EcuRed and the Council of State seat by English Wikipedia, both for 1976 without a month; January is the house default. The coordinate is corrected: the dossier gave 23.1358 / -82.3583, which points into northern Habana Vieja, and the Council of State sits in the Palacio de la Revolución on the Plaza
stops.campa: Cuba adopts a constitution, and she is elected a deputy in the first legislature of the National Assembly of People's Power and named to the Council of State. She is forty-six. Seventeen years of authority exercised through a mass organisation and a marriage acquire an office with a name, a statute and a building. The building is the Palacio de la Revolución on the Plaza, where the Council sits, three and a half kilometres from where the working material behind this file had placed it.
suggested_refs: Constitution of the Republic of Cuba, 1976, and the first legislature of the Asamblea Nacional del Poder Popular

stops.name: Copenhagen: the second world conference
stops.date_confidence: Spanish Wikipedia's international representation summary names the conference and the year. July is a default inside the year. No Cuban intervention text from Copenhagen was located
stops.campa: She leads the Cuban delegation to the mid-decade world conference on women in Copenhagen, five years on from Mexico City and five short of Nairobi. The record reached for this file names the conference and does not say one word about what she did at it, which is the shape of the record for every conference she attends over four decades. What she carries to each of them is the same document: a family code with a housework clause and a judge standing behind the clause. Whether the hall in Copenhagen found that persuasive or quaint is not written down anywhere that could be opened.
suggested_refs: Report of the World Conference of the United Nations Decade for Women, Copenhagen, 1980

stops.name: Havana: alternate to the Political Bureau
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested by Spanish Wikipedia and EcuRed. The Second Party Congress met in December 1980, and the first of that month is a default placed at the congress rather than a sourced date for her election. The geography behind this file collapsed the alternate seat and the full seat into a single 1980-1991 span; they are two steps and the second one comes in 1986
stops.campa: The party makes her an alternate member of the Political Bureau, the dozen or so people who actually decide. It is the first time her standing in the party is written down as something other than the presidency of a mass organisation, and what is written down is a half measure. She is fifty, twenty years into the Federation, and the Federation is still the instrument through which most of what she wants gets done. Alternate means present and briefed and without a vote. She holds it for six years.
suggested_refs: Second Congress of the Partido Comunista de Cuba, December 1980, Political Bureau membership

stops.name: United Nations Headquarters, New York: the General Assembly
stops.date_confidence: placeholder. English Wikipedia states that she represented Cuba at the General Assembly on women's and social issues and gives no session, no year and no speech; the source's own range is the 1970s and 1980s. The date here is a marker inside that range, not a finding, and the delegation lists that would fix it were not reachable
stops.campa: She sits in the General Assembly as a Cuban delegate on questions of women, children and the family. English Wikipedia states the role in a single clause and supplies no session, no year and no text of anything she said. Her passage through the building on the East River leaves the trace most delegates leave, which is none. The date on this stop is a marker inside a decade the source only gestures at, and it is recorded here as a gap rather than dressed up as a finding.
suggested_refs: United Nations General Assembly delegation lists for Cuba, 1970s and 1980s

stops.name: Nairobi: the third world conference
stops.date_confidence: Spanish Wikipedia's international representation summary names the conference and the year. July is a default inside the year. The Cuban delegation's interventions at Nairobi were not located
stops.campa: The United Nations decade for women closes with a conference in Nairobi, and she leads the Cuban delegation to it. She has now been to Mexico City, Copenhagen and Nairobi on the same brief, and the whole reachable record of all three amounts to three place names and three years. Did the Cuban delegation table anything at Nairobi? Spanish Wikipedia names the conference and stops. She is fifty-five and has been president of the Federation for twenty-five years.
suggested_refs: Report of the World Conference to Review and Appraise the Achievements of the United Nations Decade for Women, Nairobi, 1985

stops.name: Havana: the Third Congress, full member
stops.date_confidence: year corrected. EcuRed attaches the promotion to full Political Bureau membership to the Third Party Congress, which met in February 1986, and gives 1991 and the Fourth Congress as the end. The dossier behind this file dated the promotion to 1985; that year is wrong and is not averaged with the correct one. The day within February is a default
stops.campa: At the Third Congress of the Communist Party she is promoted from alternate to full member of the Political Bureau, and holds the seat until the Fourth Congress in 1991. For five years she sits in the room where the decisions are taken, with a vote, at the top of a state she helped make when she was twenty-eight. Several summaries put the promotion at 1985. EcuRed ties it to the Third Congress, which met in February 1986. The earlier year is an error and has not been averaged with the correct one.
suggested_refs: Third Congress of the Partido Comunista de Cuba, February 1986, Political Bureau membership

stops.name: Beijing: the fourth world conference
stops.date_confidence: Spanish Wikipedia's international representation summary names the conference and the year. September is a default inside the year. No Cuban intervention text from Beijing was located
stops.campa: The fourth world conference on women meets in Beijing and she leads Cuba's delegation, thirty-five years into the presidency of the Federation and twenty years after Mexico City. The women who ran the Federation's first literacy brigades are grandmothers now, and the family code she brought to Mexico City is old enough to have raised a generation of Cuban husbands who grew up under it. The document Beijing produces will be argued over for a generation more. She is sixty-five, and this is the last of the four.
suggested_refs: Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action, Fourth World Conference on Women, 1995

segments.name: The Mausoleum in the Sierra Cristal

stops.name: Caracas: the Order of Francisco de Miranda
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed, which gives the Orden Francisco de Miranda, first class. The coordinate is the city, not a ceremony address, which no source reached names
stops.campa: Venezuela gives her its Order of Francisco de Miranda, first class, in the years when Caracas and Havana are drawing close again after four decades in which Venezuela's governments had kept their distance from the island. The order carries the name of the Venezuelan precursor who died in a Spanish prison. Espín is seventy. EcuRed records the date and the class of the decoration and nothing whatever about the occasion, so whether she travelled to Caracas to take it in person or received it in Havana is not established here.
suggested_refs: The Orden Francisco de Miranda and its conferral records for 2001

stops.name: Palacio de la Revolución, Havana: Heroína de la República de Cuba
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed. The dossier behind this file called it the state's highest civilian honour; the title is conferred for civil and for combat merit both, and the phrasing is corrected. The coordinate repeats the corrected Palacio de la Revolución value rather than the dossier's Habana Vieja pin
stops.campa: On the second of December she is named Heroína de la República de Cuba. The date is the anniversary of the Granma landing, which she spent forty-five years earlier organising a rising in Santiago to cover, the point of the rising being to pull the police away from a beach two hundred kilometres to the west. The title is conferred for civil and for combat merit alike, which is why it fits her, rather than because of any one thing she did. She is seventy-one and still president of the Federation.
suggested_refs: The title Heroína de la República de Cuba and its statute

stops.name: Havana: the eighteenth of June
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and to the hour by English Wikipedia citing Cuban state media, which give 4:14 in the afternoon. The illness is described in reporting as prolonged and widely as cancer, which is not the same as a stated cause of death. The quotation is the official statement, read directly in the Associated Press report carried by CBS News on the same day, rather than through the New York Times obituary, which was blocked in this session
stops.campa: She dies in Havana at 4:14 in the afternoon after a long illness widely reported as cancer, seventy-seven years old, president of the Federation of Cuban Women on the day of her death as she has been on every day since August 1960. Raúl Castro is acting head of state; his brother has been out of public sight for ten months. The government issues its statement the same afternoon, in the register a state keeps for its own. Cancer is what the reporting says and not what the statement says, and no cause of death was given. That is forty-six years and ten months in one post.
stops.quote: one of the most relevant fighters for women's emancipation in our country and in the world.
stops.quote_source: Official Cuban government statement on the death of Vilma Espín, 18 June 2007, per the Associated Press report carried by CBS News, 'Wife Of Cuba's Acting Leader Dies At 77', 18 June 2007
suggested_refs: Associated Press, 'Wife Of Cuba's Acting Leader Dies At 77', 18 June 2007, carried by CBS News

stops.name: Teatro Karl Marx, Havana: the vigil
stops.date_confidence: the vigil and the mourning period are attested by English and Spanish Wikipedia, the official period running from eight in the evening of the eighteenth to ten at night on the nineteenth. Fidel Castro's absence is attested; no source reached explains it. The coordinate is corrected to the Spanish Wikipedia value for the theatre in Miramar, about 2.8 kilometres from the dossier's pin
stops.campa: The vigil is held in the Karl Marx theatre in Miramar and thousands file past. National mourning runs from eight in the evening of the eighteenth to ten at night on the nineteenth. Raúl Castro stands there through it. Fidel Castro does not come, and no source reached for this file explains the absence; his illness is the obvious answer and is not the same thing as a stated one. The Colombian ELN sends a letter of condolence signed by its whole central command.
suggested_refs: Cuban state media coverage of the mourning decree of 18-19 June 2007

stops.name: Mayarí Arriba, Sierra Cristal: the ashes at the Second Front
stops.date_confidence: the cremation and interment at the Mausoleo del Segundo Frente Oriental Frank País are attested by English and Spanish Wikipedia; only the month is given, and the twentieth follows the vigil of the nineteenth as an inference. The coordinate is the worst correction in this file: the dossier's afterlife lens gave 20.05 / -75.7333, about 44 kilometres from the Segundo Frente municipal seat, and its geography lens gave 20.4761 / -75.6247, about 13 kilometres off. No published coordinate for the mausoleum itself, as distinct from the seat at Mayarí Arriba, was located
stops.campa: Her body is cremated and the ashes are placed in the mausoleum of the Second Eastern Front, in the mountains where she served her six months under Raúl Castro's command. The mausoleum carries Frank País's name. Frank País is not in it: he lies in the Santa Ifigenia cemetery in Santiago, with José Martí, and from 2016 with Fidel Castro. She is buried under her mentor's name and not beside him, in the range where the front was, which is the Sierra Cristal and not the Sierra Maestra.
suggested_refs: Mausoleo del Segundo Frente Oriental Frank País, inaugurated 11 March 1978, Segundo Frente municipality

stops.name: Havana: the school and the book
stops.date_confidence: the school naming is attested to April 2013 by English Wikipedia, without a day. The book is corrected: the dossier gave the title as Cuban Women, and the Pathfinder Press catalogue gives Women in Cuba: The Making of a Revolution Within the Revolution, English edition 2012, with a Farsi edition of 2021. The absence of a statue is an absence in the material reached, not a demonstrated absence
stops.campa: A primary school in Havana opens under her name in April. The year before, Pathfinder Press had brought out Women in Cuba: The Making of a Revolution Within the Revolution, her speeches together with those of Asela de los Santos and Yolanda Ferrer, the main English edition of her political writing; a Farsi translation follows in 2021. The Federation she founded still publishes Mujeres. No statue turned up in any source reached, and no freestanding monument, which is an absence in the material opened here rather than a demonstrated absence in Cuba.
suggested_refs: Vilma Espín, Asela de los Santos and Yolanda Ferrer, Women in Cuba: The Making of a Revolution Within the Revolution (Pathfinder Press, 2012)
